stem.text: A potentiometer and a driver cell of electromotive force (e.m.f.) $E$ are used to measure the e.m.f. of a new cell.
A sliding contact at P is moved along a resistance wire QR until the reading on the galvanometer is zero.

stem.alt: Potentiometer circuit diagram. A driver cell labelled E is in the top branch of a rectangular loop. A horizontal resistance wire runs from Q at the left to R at the right, with a sliding contact labelled P above it connected to a galvanometer. A new cell is in the lower branch, connected to Q and to the galvanometer.

stem.text: What is an essential requirement for the e.m.f. of the new cell to be measured accurately?

A.text: The e.m.f. of the driver cell must be less than the e.m.f. of the new cell.

B.text: The galvanometer must have a large resistance.

C.text: The internal resistance of the new cell must be zero.

D.text: The resistance per unit length of the wire QR must be constant.
